Q: CS0246 Type or namespace "Newtonsoft" not found A:

It's recommended to use one of the prepared Newtonsoft.Json forks that have changed it to be compatible with Unity3D. They are much easier to use than the NuGet package, and unlike the official NuGet package that will fail at runtime when building to AOT targets such as Android, iOS, WebGL, etc., they all have support for this. Here are the top three:

  • jilleJr/Newtonsoft.Json-for-Unity, Newtonsoft.Json 12.0.1-12.0.3, available via the Unity Package Manager (UPM) that's built-in Unity 2018.1 and upwards.

  • SaladLab/Json.Net.Unity, Newtonsoft.Json 7.0.1-9.0.1, available via .unitypackage and UniGet

  • ParentElement's JSON .NET for Unity, Newtonsoft.Json 8.0.3, available via the Unity Assets Store

The variant by jilleJr is the only active fork at time of writing. The others has stopped development.

Installation instructions taken from jilleJr's wiki

Open /Packages/manifest.json, add scope for jillejr, then add the package in the list of dependencies.

À la:

{
  "scopedRegistries": [
    {
      "name": "Packages from jillejr",
      "url": "https://npm.cloudsmith.io/jillejr/newtonsoft-json-for-unity/",
      "scopes": ["jillejr"]
    }
  ],
  "dependencies": {
    "jillejr.newtonsoft.json-for-unity": "12.0.201",

    // ...
  }
}

// ... signals the rest of the packages you have in the manifest.json, such as all the "com.unity.*" dependencies

Q: How to sum a calculated measure? A:

I found the easiest way to do this:

  1. Create a new named calculation in the appropriate measure table in your DSV. (Right click, add new named calculation and set its expression to be CAST(NULL as [insert appropriate data type]).
  2. Add the new named calculation as a measure in your cube.
  3. In the calculations area of your cube switch to script view and add the following:

({[Measures].[The named calculation you created in step 1]},Leaves())=Your complex calculation;

This sets the definition at the leaf level and all the aggregations work perfectly.

Ref: http://sqlblog.com/blogs/mosha/archive/2005/02/13/performance-of-aggregating-data-from-lower-levels-in-mdx.aspx

Q: How to add Paste button in UIMenu such that the system "allow app to paste" prompt does not appear A:

Creating a UIAction with the .paste or .newFromPasteboard identifier will suppress the system prompt if the user taps the action in the menu. It will not be suppressed in other scenarios like if the user long presses the button to open the menu, swipes up to the action, then releases to activate it. This was stated by a DTS engineer on the Apple Developer Forums and confirmed by me (using iOS 26.5). The code in the question exhibits this behavior.

Q: Meaning of `command < <(command)`? A:

Technically, I don't believe it makes a temporary file. It makes a file path, but the "file" is actually a named pipe (or a quasi-unnamed pipe tied to /dev/fd). The definition is squicky, since this is the whole UNIX "everything is a file" paradigm, but I make the distinction because with a pipe, named or otherwise, the data is never stored to disk, it merely has a name on disk where interacting with said name sends data in-memory between processes.

Q: Yum crashed with a keyboard interrupt error A:

This issue happens when the user upgrades to Python 3. Just simply edit the file --> /usr/bin/yum and change to first line to --> "#!/usr/bin/python2"

If the above solution wouldn't solve all YUM dependency problems, its better to run the below commands.

sudo ln -s /usr/local/bin/python3 /usr/bin/python3 # Mark latest Python as Python 3

sudo ln -sf /usr/bin/python2.7 /usr/bin/python (make 2.7 as the default Python interpreter)
